sources.title: Scale-Dependent Habitat Selection and Size-Based Dominance in Adult Male American Alligators
sources.locator: Abstract; Methods, Study Area and Radio-telemetry; Results; Discussion.
sources.scope: Primary field study of 17 adult male Alligator mississippiensis tracked along the Pearl River and Ross Barnett Reservoir in central Mississippi during 2012–2013; 1,145 locations were analyzed.
sources.license: CC0 public-domain dedication, stated in the article copyright section.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Copyright/license statement after article citation; CC0 dedication.
sources.attribution: Strickland BA, Vilella FJ, Belant JL (2016). Scale-Dependent Habitat Selection and Size-Based Dominance in Adult Male American Alligators. PLoS ONE 11(9):e0161814. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0161814. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: Seventeen adult males tracked on the Pearl River and Ross Barnett Reservoir in 2012–2013 contributed 1,145 locations to home-range and patch-scale habitat-selection analyses.
claims.scope: Adult males at one Mississippi river-reservoir system only.

claims.text: Habitat selection differed across spatial scales; body size was not associated with home-range size or resource selection in this sample.
claims.scope: Study-area, sample, and time limits apply; no species-wide behavior or dominance claim.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
The study does not assess females, juveniles, other populations, full distribution, or current conservation status.
